warnings.title: Нацкиберуправление Израиля предупреждает о поддельных сообщениях от полиции
warnings.summary: Национальное управление кибербезопасности Израиля предупреждает о фишинговых сообщениях, которые выдают себя за полицию и требуют оплатить несуществующий штраф за нарушение ПДД по ссылке. Мошенники угрожают дополнительными штрафами, чтобы заставить жертву действовать быстро.
warnings.he_original:
⚠️ מערך הסייבר הלאומי מתריע: הודעת התחזות למשטרת ישראל

בשעות האחרונות מופצת הודעה המתחזה למשטרת ישראל וטוענת כי קיים דוח תנועה על שם הנמען. ההודעה מפנה לקישור לתשלום ומאיימת בקנסות נוספים אם לא ישולם בזמן.

מדובר בניסיון התחזות. גם מספר דוח שמופיע בהודעה אינו הוכחה לאמינותה. אל תתנו ללחץ לתשלום להחליף בדיקה.

איך מתגוננים?

🔹 לא לוחצים על הקישור ולא מוסרים פרטים אישיים, פרטי אשראי או קודי אימות.

🔹 לפני שמשלמים, נכנסים ישירות לדף השירות הרשמי ״תשלום קנסות תעבורה״ באתר gov.il ופועלים לפי ההנחיות שבו:
https://www.gov.il/he/service/police_fine_payment⁠

🔹 קיבלתם קישור חשוד? העתיקו אותו בלי לפ…
warnings.ru_translation:
⚠️ Национальное управление кибербезопасности предупреждает: поддельное сообщение от полиции Израиля

В последние часы распространяется сообщение, выдающее себя за полицию Израиля, в котором утверждается, что на имя получателя существует отчет о нарушении ПДД. Сообщение содержит ссылку для оплаты и угрожает дополнительными штрафами, если оплата не будет произведена вовремя.

Это попытка выдать себя за другое лицо. Даже номер отчета, указанный в сообщении, не является доказательством его достоверности. Не позволяйте давлению необходимости оплаты заменить проверку.

Как защититься?

🔹 Не нажимайте на ссылку и не сообщайте личные данные, данные кредитной карты или коды подтверждения.

🔹 Прежде чем платить, зайдите напрямую на официальную страницу услуги «Оплата штрафов за нарушение ПДД» на сайте gov.il и действуйте согласно инструкциям на ней:
https://www.gov.il/he/service/police_fine_payment

🔹 Получили подозрительную ссылку? Скопируйте её, не открывая, и проверьте через сервис «Click Check» на портале национальной кибербезопасности:
https://portal.cyber.gov.il/clickcheck

Уже сообщили данные кредитной карты?
Немедленно обратитесь в кредитную компанию или банк по официальному каналу, сообщите о подозрении на мошенничество и получите инструкции по защите карты и проверке списаний.

📞 Для сообщения и помощи: звоните 119 в Национальное управление кибербезопасности.
👍3❤1
warnings.what_to_notice: В этом случае должно насторожить: сообщение приходит якобы от полиции Израиля, но содержит ссылку для оплаты и угрозу дополнительных штрафов — официальные органы не рассылают такие уведомления через случайные сообщения со ссылками. Наличие номера отчета в сообщении не гарантирует подлинность, так как номер может быть выдуман или скопирован. Давление на срочность оплаты — типичный прием мошенников, чтобы жертва не проверила информацию. Ссылка ведет не на официальный сайт gov.il, а на сторонний ресурс. Также запрашиваются личные данные, данные карты или коды подтверждения, что никогда не требуется при оплате через официальный портал.

warnings.summary: Attackers send messages with a link to a fake website that imitates Google Play and offer to install the Tax Administration application for Android. איך מתגוננים?

🔹 מורידים אפליקציות רק מהחנות הרשמית שבמכשיר, בכניסה עצמאית.
🔹 לא מתקינים אפליקציות מקישורים בהודעות ולא מאשרים התקנה ממקור לא מוכר.
🔹 בודקים פניות בכניסה עצמאית לאתר הרשמי של רשות המסים.
🔹 קיבלתם קישור חשוד? העתיקו אותו בלי לפתוח ובדקו בשירות ״קליק צ׳ק״ בפורטל הס…
warnings.ru_translation: ⚠️National Cyber ​​Security Administration Warns: Malicious app impersonating IRS. The department has received reports of messages that lead to a website that imitates the Google Play Store and offers an app called “Tax Office” for Android devices. A management investigation revealed that once installed and granted permissions, the app could allow attackers to access messages, verification codes and the camera, as well as remotely control the device. How to protect yourself? 🔹 Download applications only from the official store on your device by logging into it yourself. 🔹 Do not install applications using links from messages and do not confirm installation from an unknown source. 🔹 Check applications by going to the official website of the Tax Administration yourself. 🔹 Received a suspicious link? Copy it without opening it and check it through the Click-Check service on the national cybersecurity portal: https://portal.cyber.gov.il/clickcheck Already installed? Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data, and avoid entering passwords or banking on your device. From another uninfected device, change passwords and disconnect devices that you do not recognize from accounts. Deleting the application is not enough. It is recommended to perform a full factory reset and install applications only from official stores, without automatically restoring them from an old backup. 📞 For messages and assistance: call 119 National Cyber ​​Security Authority. ❤4👍2
warnings.what_to_notice: What should be alarming is that the link to the application comes in a message and does not lead directly to the official Google Play. The site itself imitates the Google Play store, but is not it. The app uses the name “IRS,” although official government agencies do not distribute their apps through links in messages. Once installed, it asks for permissions to access SMS, verification codes, and the camera, which is unusual for an IRS app. Installation from an unknown source is also suggested.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.summary: Israel's National Cyber ​​Security Authority warns of a fraudulent email posing as Yad2: the message leads to a fake app store site that offers to download and install a suspicious application from an unknown source.
warnings.he_original:
⚠️ מערך הסייבר הלאומי מתריע: ניסיון התחזות ליד2 באמצעות אפליקציה חשודה

במערך הסייבר הלאומי התקבל דיווח על הודעה המתחזה ליד2, ומפנה להורדת אפליקציה לצורך השלמת הזמנה ומשלוח.

הקישור מוביל לאתר מזויף המדמה חנות אפליקציות, כולל דירוגים ומספר הורדות, ומבקש מהמשתמש להוריד קובץ ולאשר התקנה ממקור לא מוכר.

שימו לב: מדובר בניסיון התחזות, והאפליקציה החשודה נמצאת בבדיקה.

איך מתגוננים?

🔹 מורידים אפליקציות רק מהחנויות הרשמיות, Google Play ו-App Store, ולא מקישורים שמתקבלים בהודעות.

warnings.ru_translation: ⚠️National Cyber ​​Security Authority Warns: Attempt to impersonate Yad2 using suspicious app The National Cyber ​​Security Authority has received a report of an attempt to impersonate Yad2 through a message that directs people to download an app to complete an order and delivery. The link leads to a fake site that imitates an app store, including ratings and download numbers, and asks the user to download a file and confirm installation from an unknown source. Please note: this is an attempt to impersonate another person, and the suspicious application is under review. How to protect yourself? 🔹 Download applications only from the official Google Play and App Store, and not from links received in messages. 🔹 Are they asking to “allow installation from this source”? Do not allow or continue the installation. 🔹 Check what permissions the application requests and whether they are appropriate for its use. Remember: even a site that looks like an official app store can be fake. Have you received a suspicious message or already installed the application? Report to the National Cyber ​​Security Administration's 119 Center.
warnings.what_to_notice: In this case, the following should be on your guard: the message supposedly comes from Yad2 with a requirement to complete the order and delivery - this is a typical social engineering technique that creates urgency. The link does not lead to the official store, but to a fake website that imitates an app store, including fake ratings and download numbers to appear authentic. The user is then asked to download a file and confirm installation from an unknown source - this is a direct sign of malware. It's also worth checking what permissions the app is asking for: if they don't match its function, it's suspicious.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

שנים של פיתוח. רגע אחד של החלטה. ואולי לא תהיה הזדמנות שנייה.

לקראת כנס Cyber Week בשבוע הבא, שי גל מארח את מייסד הכנס, אלוף (במיל׳) פרופ׳ יצחק בן ישראל, בפרק השלישי של ״בלי ירייה אחת״, הפודקאסט של מערך הסייבר הלאומי.

שיחה על רעיון שנשמע פעם כמו מדע בדיוני: לחדור למחשבי האויב לא רק כדי לאסוף מידע, אלא כדי לשבש את פעולתו מבפנים.

איך בונים יכולת כזו, מתי מחליטים להפעיל אותה, ואיך מגנים על המדינה ותשתיותיה בעולם שהופך יותר ויותר דיגיטלי?

הכנס יתקיים באוניברסיטת תל אביב בשותפות המערך ובהשתתפות ראש המערך, תא״ל (במיל׳) יוסי כראדי, ורבים מנשות ואנשי המערך.

עד שניפגש בכנס, קבלו הצצה לפרק 🎬
🎧 ״…
warnings.ru_translation: Years of development. One moment of decision. And perhaps there won't be a second chance. Ahead of next week's Cyber ​​Week conference, Shai Gal is hosting the conference's founder, Maj. Gen. (ret.) Prof. Yitzhak Ben-Israel, in the third episode of the National Cyber ​​Security Administration's Without a Shot Podcast. Talk about an idea that once sounded like science fiction: infiltrating enemy computers not only to gather information, but also to disrupt their operation from the inside. How do they create such an opportunity, when they decide to use it, and how do they protect the state and its infrastructure in a world that is becoming increasingly digital? The conference will take place at Tel Aviv University in partnership with the Office and with the participation of the head of the Office, Brigadier General (ret.) Yossi Karadi, and many members of the Office's staff. See you at the conference, get a taste of the episode 🎬 🎧 “The Weapon You Can't Use Twice” To watch and listen to the full episode on Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/episode/5LwLRBYJvM1ZPJL5wQkW38?si=JGQsN0FbRbKy8w6VlInRdg&utm_source=copy-link 👍2❤1👎1🙏1
warnings.what_to_notice: The link leads to Spotify with tracking parameters (utm_source=copy-link), which is typical for bulk emails. Mentioning high-ranking officials (Prof. Ben-Israel, General Karadi) creates trust. Emojis and the “get the idea” message can encourage conversion. Official National Cyber ​​Security Administration accounts typically do not use such links in posts. Reactions (👍2❤1👎1🙏1) look like an artificial boost.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.title: Israel's National Cyber ​​Security Authority has launched a portal with free security tools
warnings.summary: Israel's National Cyber ​​Security Authority has unveiled an official portal with free tools for checking suspicious links, learning to recognize phishing, and assessing the level of protection. The portal is available at portal.cyber.gov.il.
warnings.he_original:
🛡️ הגנת הסייבר שלכם, עכשיו בכף היד&#33;

קיבלתם קישור חשוד? רוצים לדעת עד כמה אתם מוגנים ברשת? מעכשיו יש מקום אחד שבו תוכלו לבדוק, ללמוד ולהתגונן.

מערך הסייבר הלאומי משיק את פורטל הסייבר הלאומי, עם מגוון כלים ושירותים חינמיים לאזרחים, לעסקים ולארגונים.

📊 למה זה חשוב? בשנה האחרונה זוהתה עלייה של כ-145% במתקפות פישינג, ומתחילת 2026 התקבלו במערך יותר מ-26 אלף דיווחים על חשדות למתקפות סייבר.

מה מחכה לכם בפורטל?

🔗 קליק צ’ק: בודקים קישורים חשודים בלי לפתוח אותם, ומקבלים הערכה לגבי מידת מהימנותם.

🎮 זהה את המתחזה: משחק אינטראקטיבי לזיהוי הודעות פישינג.

🔐 בדיקת רמת ההגנה: מגלים עד כמה אתם מוגנ…
warnings.ru_translation: 🛡️ Your cyber protection is now in the palm of your hand! Received a suspicious link? Want to know how secure you are online? From now on, there is one place where you can test, learn and protect yourself. The National Cyber ​​Security Authority is launching a National Cyber ​​Portal with a variety of free tools and services for citizens, businesses and organizations. 📊 Why is this important? Over the past year, an increase of approximately 145% in phishing attacks has been detected, and since the beginning of 2026, the department has received more than 26 thousand reports of suspected cyber attacks. What awaits you on the portal? 🔗 Click-check: check suspicious links without opening them and get an assessment of their reliability. 🎮 Recognize the impostor: an interactive game to identify phishing messages. 🔐 Check your protection level: find out how protected you are and what needs to be improved. 🚨 Cyber ​​Alerts: Stay up to date with threats and protection recommendations. 🏢 For businesses and organizations: security checks, professional tools and targeted alerts. Everything is in one place, free and for everyone. We invite you to come in, try it and start protecting yourself. 👉 National cyber portal: https://portal.cyber.gov.il 👍3
warnings.what_to_notice: This is an official post from a government agency and not a fraudulent message. However, attackers can fake such announcements: in this case, the portal.cyber.gov.il domain belongs to the Israeli government (gov.il), which confirms the authenticity. Signs of counterfeit in possible copies: a similar but not exact domain (for example, cyber.gov.il.portal.com or portal-cyber-gov.il), calls to follow shortened links, requests for personal information or payment. This portal is free and does not require you to enter sensitive information for basic checks.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application

warnings.title: Israeli National Cyber ​​Authority: automated calls on behalf of Google
warnings.summary: Israel's National Cyber ​​Security Authority is warning about fraudulent robocalls in English that are posing as Google's account hack warnings and require urgent action. The agency urges you not to follow the call instructions, but to check your account yourself and report such cases to 119.
warnings.he_original:
⚠️ מערך הסייבר הלאומי מתריע: שיחות אוטומטיות המתחזות לגוגל

במערך הסייבר הלאומי מתקבלים דיווחים על שיחות באנגלית המתחזות להתרעת אבטחה של גוגל. בהודעה נטען שמספר הטלפון בחשבון השתנה ושהפעילות מקורה בטהראן, איראן.

אל תתנו להודעה המלחיצה לגרום לכם לפעול ללא בדיקה. עצם קבלת השיחה אינה הוכחה שהחשבון נפרץ.

🔹 לא מקישים על מספרים ולא ממשיכים בשיחה החשודה. מנתקים.
🔹 לא מוסרים סיסמאות וקודי אימות ולא מאשרים פעולות שלא יזמתם.
🔹 בודקים את החשבון באופן עצמאי באפליקציה או באתר הרשמי של גוגל, ולא באמצעות קישור או מספר שנמסרו בפנייה.

קיבלתם שיחה כזו או שכבר מסרתם פרטים? פנו למוקד 119 של מערך הסייבר הלאו…
warnings.ru_translation: ⚠️ National Cyber ​​Security Administration Warns: Robocalls Impersonating Google The National Cyber ​​Security Administration is receiving reports of calls in English posing as Google security alerts. The message claims that the phone number on the account has been changed and the activity is coming from Tehran, Iran. Don't let a warning message cause you to act without checking. The mere fact of receiving a call is not proof that the account has been hacked. 🔹 Do not click on the numbers and do not continue the suspicious conversation. Hang up. 🔹 Do not share passwords or verification codes or confirm actions that you did not initiate. 🔹 Check your account yourself in the application or on the official Google website, and not using the link or number provided in the appeal. Have you received such a call or have you already provided information? Contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration's 119 Center for reporting and consultation. 👍8❤3😨1
warnings.what_to_notice: You should be wary of: a call in English with an automatic voice, which appears to be the Google security service; the statement about changing the phone number in the account and activity from Tehran (Iran) - this creates a false sense of urgency and threat; please press numbers or continue the conversation; requesting passwords or verification codes; an offer to follow a link or call the number specified in the message itself. Genuine Google does not call with such warnings or ask for passwords or codes. The mere fact of a call does not mean a hack.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.title: Israel warns: Fraudsters use AI to spoof online stores
warnings.summary: Israel's National Cyber ​​Security Authority warns that fraudsters are using AI to create convincing fake online stores. Citizens are urged to check sellers, not to provide card details and confirmation codes, and to check delivery status only on official websites.
warnings.he_original:
🛒 המחיר יורד? אל תורידו את ההגנות

חודש הקניות כבר כאן. הבינה המלאכותית יכולה לעזור למצוא מבצעים, אבל גם להפוך אתרי קניות מתחזים למשכנעים יותר. אז לפני שממלאים את העגלה, עוצרים לבדיקה:
🔹 בודקים איפה קונים. נכנסים ישירות לאתר או לאפליקציה הרשמית ובודקים מי עומד מאחורי החנות. מחיר נמוך באופן חריג ולחץ לשלם מיד? סיבה לעצור.

🔹 נעזרים ב־AI, אבל לא סומכים בעיניים עצומות. מאמתים את החנות והמחיר, ולא משתפים בצ׳אט פרטי אשראי, סיסמאות או קודי אימות.

🔹 מגנים על התשלום. לא מוסרים קוד אימות לאיש ומפעילים התראות על חיובים.

🔹 מחכים לחבילה? בודקים את מצב המשלוח באתר הרשמי של חברת המשלוחים, ולא דרך קישור…
warnings.ru_translation: 🛒 Is the price going down? Don't turn off your protection Shopping Month is here. Artificial intelligence can help you find discounts, but it can also make fake shopping sites more convincing. Therefore, before filling your cart, stop to check: 🔹 We check where we buy. We go directly to the official website or app and check who is behind the store. Unusually low price and pressure to pay immediately? Reason to stop. 🔹 We use AI, but we don’t trust blindly. We check the store and price, and do not share credit card information, passwords or verification codes in the chat. 🔹 We protect the payment. We do not share the confirmation code with anyone and enable notifications about charges. 🔹 Are you waiting for the package? We check the delivery status on the official website of the delivery company, and not via the link in the received message. Additional recommendations from the National Cybersecurity Directorate for safe online shopping, including in the era of artificial intelligence 👇 https://www.gov.il/he/pages/shop011126 ❤2
warnings.what_to_notice: You should be wary of: unusually low prices and pressure to pay immediately; going to the store’s website via a link from a message or advertisement, and not directly; lack of information about the store owner; please provide your credit card details, password or confirmation code in the chat; notification of a parcel with a link that does not lead to the official website of the delivery company. Scammers use AI to make fake sites look believable, so you can't rely on visual impressions alone.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.title: Israel's National Cyber ​​Authority: Protecting Election Systems, Not Warning About Fraud

מגנים בסייבר על החגיגה הדמוקרטית 🇮🇱

אחרי חודשים של היערכות ועבודה מאומצת, מערך הסייבר הלאומי ושותפיו פועלים יחד להגנה על המערכות הקשורות לתהליך הבחירות, כדי לסייע בשמירה על מהלכו התקין.

warnings.what_to_notice: This post does not contain any requests, links, attachments or requests for personal information - this is an official informational message. warnings.title: Israel launches Operation Election Shield to protect digital systems
warnings.summary: Israel's National Cybersecurity Authority and the Central Election Commission have announced Operation Election Shield to protect digital systems serving elections. Citizens are advised to check information only on official websites, beware of disturbing links and report hacked sites to the 119 center.
warnings.he_original:
🛡️ מגינים על הבחירות: יוצאים למבצע ״מגן הבחירות״

מערך הסייבר הלאומי וועדת הבחירות המרכזית הכריזו על מבצע להגנת המערכות הדיגיטליות התומכות בתהליך הבחירות. ההכרזה באה בתום פגישה של ראש המערך, יוסי כראדי, עם יו״ר ועדת הבחירות המרכזית, השופט נעם סולברג, ועם מ״מ מנכ״ל הוועדה, עו״ד דין ליבנה.

ההצבעה בישראל נעשית בפתקי נייר. המבצע נועד להגן על המערכות שמאחורי התהליך, וכולל חיזוק ההגנה, ניטור מוגבר ואיתור מוקדם של איומים. ביום הבחירות יפעל מרכז מצב סייבר ייעודי למענה מהיר לאירועים חריגים.

המלצות לציבור:

* בדקו מידע על הבחירות ישירות באתרים הרשמיים.
* היזהרו מקישורים בהודעות שמנסות להלחיץ או לזר…
warnings.ru_translation: 🛡️ Protecting elections: launching Operation Election Shield The National Cybersecurity Directorate and the Central Election Commission announced an operation to protect digital systems supporting the electoral process. The announcement was made following a meeting between the head of the Office, Yossi Karadi, and the Chairman of the Central Election Commission, Judge Noam Solberg, and the acting. the commission's general director, lawyer Dean Livne. Voting in Israel is carried out using paper ballots. The operation is designed to protect the systems behind the process and includes hardening, enhanced monitoring and early detection of threats. On Election Day, a special cyber situation center will operate to quickly respond to abnormal incidents. Recommendations for the public: * Check election information directly on official websites. * Beware of links in posts that try to scare or push you. * Check unusual messages before sharing them. * Have you encountered a hacked website? Close your browser and report to the National Cyber ​​Security Administration's 119 Center. Photo: Meir Amzaleg, for the press. 👍12
warnings.what_to_notice: In this case, the warning comes from an official source and concerns election cybersecurity. You should be wary of fake messages or sites imitating official resources about elections: links in SMS or instant messengers that rush, scare or require urgent action (for example, “check if your vote has been deleted”, “confirm your data urgently”). Signs of a fake: unofficial domain, lack of connection with the websites of the Central Election Commission or the National Cybersecurity Directorate, grammatical errors, calls to follow a link from an alarm message. It is also dangerous to share unverified screenshots or hacking reports - only distribute information from official sites. If the site appears to be hacked, do not interact with it, close your browser and report to the 119 center.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.title: Israeli Cyber ​​Security Warns of Scams on behalf of Binance and Other Platforms
warnings.summary: Israel's National Cyber ​​Security Authority warns of fraudulent calls and SMS messages in which attackers impersonate Binance and other well-known platforms to scam personal and account information. It is recommended not to call back, not to share passwords or codes, and to check your account only through official applications or websites.
warnings.he_original:
שימו לב: ניסיונות התחזות בשם Binance ופלטפורמות מוכרות נוספות

בימים האחרונים התקבלו במערך הסייבר הלאומי דיווחים על שיחות ומסרונים שמטרתם לדלות מידע אישי ופרטי חשבון.

בחלק מהמקרים ההודעה מופיעה בתוך שרשור שנראה לגיטימי, טוענת לניסיון התחברות חריג ומפנה למספר טלפון שבו מתחזה מבקש פרטי דוא”ל, חשבונות פיננסיים או פרטי התחברות.

מערך הסייבר הלאומי ממליץ:

• לא לחזור למספר שמופיע בהודעה חשודה.
• לא למסור סיסמאות, קודי אימות או פרטי חשבון.
• לא להקיש מספרים או לאשר פעולה בשיחה שלא יזמתם.
• לבדוק את החשבון רק דרך האפליקציה או האתר הרשמי.

זכרו: גם הודעה שמופיעה בתוך שרשור מוכר אינה בהכרח לגיטימית.
warnings.ru_translation: Warning: attempts to impersonate Binance and other well-known platforms In recent days, the National Cyber ​​Security Administration has received reports of calls and SMS messages aimed at extorting personal information and account data. In some cases, the message appears inside a conversation thread that appears to be legitimate, claims an unusual login attempt, and directs to a phone number where the impersonator asks for email, financial account, or login information. The National Cyber ​​Security Administration recommends: • Do not call back the number listed in a suspicious message. • Do not share passwords, verification codes, or account information. • Do not press numbers or confirm an action in a call that you did not initiate. • Check your account only through the official application or website. Remember: even a message that appears in a familiar conversation thread is not necessarily legitimate.
warnings.what_to_notice: In this case, you should be wary: 1) The message comes inside an existing correspondence thread, which creates a false sense of legitimacy, but in fact, scammers can forge or infiltrate message chains. 2) The statement about 'unusual input' is a typical social engineering technique that causes anxiety and a desire to act immediately. 3) Redirect to a phone number asking for email, financial account or login details - real companies never ask for such information over the phone. 4) Please provide passwords, verification codes or account information. 5) Please press numbers or confirm an action in a call that you did not initiate. 6) Even if a message looks like part of a familiar correspondence, this does not guarantee its authenticity.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.title: Microsoft: Israel is second in the world in cyber attacks, threats are growing
warnings.summary: A Microsoft report puts Israel in second place in the world for cyberattacks. With threats growing and AI accelerating attacks, the head of the National Cyber ​​Security Administration warns that defenses must continually evolve.
warnings.he_original:
דוח Microsoft החדש: ישראל במקום השני בעולם במתקפות סייבר

דוח ההגנה הדיגיטלית החדש של Microsoft מציב את ישראל במקום השני בעולם והראשון במזרח התיכון במדד מתקפות הסייבר.

הנתונים ממחישים את עוצמת האיום שעמו מתמודדת ישראל, אך גם את חשיבותו של החוסן הלאומי: היכולת להגן על אזרחים ושירותים חיוניים, לצמצם נזק ולשמור על רציפות תפקודית גם תחת מתקפות מתמשכות.

החוסן הזה נשען על מערכת הגנה לאומית משולבת ועל שיתוף פעולה בין מערך הסייבר הלאומי, גופי הביטחון, משרדי הממשלה, המשק, תעשיית הסייבר והחברות הגלובליות.

ראש מערך הסייבר הלאומי, יוסי כראדי:

“האיומים מתגברים, והבינה המלאכותית משנה את פני המערכה בס…
warnings.ru_translation: New Microsoft report: Israel ranks second in the world for cyberattacks Microsoft's new report on digital security ranks Israel second in the world and first in the Middle East for cyberattacks. The data demonstrates the strength of the threat Israel faces, but also the importance of national resilience: the ability to protect citizens and vital services, reduce damage, and maintain functional continuity even under continuous attack. This resilience relies on a comprehensive national defense system and collaboration between the National Cyber ​​Security Authority, security agencies, government ministries, the economy, the cyber industry and global companies. National Cybersecurity Director Yossi Karadi: “Threats are intensifying, and artificial intelligence is changing the face of cyber warfare and accelerating the pace of attacks. There is no ceasefire in cyberspace, so defense must constantly evolve.” As the threats and changes brought by artificial intelligence increase, defense capabilities must continue to be adapted, collaboration strengthened, and national readiness enhanced. 👍9
warnings.what_to_notice: This is an official post from Israel's National Cyber ​​Security Authority and not a scam. warnings.title: Cybersecurity: how to protect yourself from indirect injection into AI assistants
warnings.summary: Fraudsters can embed hidden instructions into the content processed by the AI ​​assistant to trick it into performing malicious actions. Users should limit AI permissions and require manual confirmation for sensitive transactions.
warnings.he_original:

כאן נכנסת לתמונה Indirect Prompt Injection: התוקף שותל באתר, במסמך או במייל הוראה שמיועדת לעוזר ה-AI, ולעיתים מסתיר אותה מהעין.

אתם מבקשים: “סכם לי את העמוד הזה”.

warnings.ru_translation: The attacker is not always trying to trick you. Sometimes it tries to trick your AI. 🤖⚠️ AI assistants can read emails, summarize websites and documents, access calendars, and perform actions on behalf of the user. This is where indirect prompt injection comes into play: the attacker embeds an instruction intended for an AI assistant on a website, document, or email, and sometimes hides it from view. You ask: “Summarize this page for me.” But another instruction may appear inside the page: ignore the task, disclose information, or perform an additional action. If the assistant has broad rights, he can send information, change data, or perform actions in the account. warnings.ru_translation: ⚠️ LockBit Attack Attempts: How to Mitigate the Risk Recently, the National Cyber ​​Security Authority has received reports of LockBit ransomware attack attempts and threats against organizations in Israel. Attackers use phishing, stolen passwords, and security vulnerabilities to infiltrate systems, steal information, and encrypt files. How to reduce the risk: 🔹 Enable two-factor authentication for remote access and change user passwords 🔹 Regularly update operating systems, software and servers 🔹 Do not open links or files from unknown sources 🔹 Restrict access to VPN and administrative interfaces using VPNs, IP whitelists or a ZTNA solution, and avoid them directly to the Internet 🔹 Keep current backup copies isolated from the network and check the possibility of recovering data from them Are you afraid that you have been damaged? ❗ Immediately disconnect your computer from the network and the Internet ❗ Do not turn on your computer again or try to recover files yourself ❗ Do not delete files or the ransom message ❗ Contact a professional immediately and report to the National Cyber ​​Security Administration 119 Center A quick response can reduce the extent of the damage and prevent the ransomware from spreading to other computers and servers. ❤5👍3👏1😈1

warnings.ru_translation: ⚠️ The National Cyber ​​Security Administration is warning of a phishing campaign posing as a financial document submission to SharePoint. מספר המקומות מוגבל ומותנה בקבלת אישור להשתתפות. 

🔗 לבקשת השתתפות נא למלא הטופס עד 25.8.26:
https://forms.monday.com/forms/503ffde09cff429f45aa93b03241b752?r=euc1
warnings.ru_translation: Executives and key employees of the Israeli cyber industry, come take part in a unique meeting with the head of the National Cyber ​​Security Authority! The focus is on a national cyber campaign. In a day when cyberspace is front and center, the partnership between the National Cyber ​​Security Administration and the cyber defense industry has never been more important! At the meeting we will present an up-to-date picture of national trends and discuss common challenges. Come listen, have your say and influence the discussion. The number of places is limited and requires confirmation of participation. 🔗 To apply for participation, fill out the form before 25.8.26: https://forms.monday.com/forms/503ffde09cff429f45aa93b03241b752?r=euc1
warnings.what_to_notice: Please note: the link is to forms.monday.com and not to the official Israeli government website (eg gov.il). The form asks for personal information, which is typical for phishing scams. Also the date 8/25/26 looks unrealistic (next year). Official invitations from government agencies are usually sent from official domains and do not require filling out third-party forms.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.title: Warning about phishing attacks targeting journalists and public figures in Israel
warnings.summary: Israeli intelligence agencies are warning of an increase in phishing attacks against journalists and public figures. It is recommended to be vigilant, do not click on suspicious links, enable two-factor authentication, and report suspicious attempts.
warnings.he_original:
שירות הביטחון הכללי ומערך הסייבר הלאומי מדווחים על עלייה בניסיונות למתקפות פישינג המוכוונות לעיתונאים ישראלים וגורמים נוספים העוסקים בפעילות ציבורית. המערך והשירות זיהו את הנסיונות ופועלים כדי למנועם ולסכלם. 

המלצות מערך הסייבר הלאומי להגנה על החשבונות: 
• אימות זהות הפונה באמצעי תקשורת נוסף.
• אין להזין סיסמאות או קודי אימות בעקבות קישור שהתקבל בהודעה, גם לא כדי להתחבר לשיחת וידאו.
• הפעלת אימות דו-שלבי בכל החשבונות המרכזיים.
• ביצוע בדיקה תקופתית של ההתחברות לחשבונות והסרת מכשירים או חיבורים שאינם מוכרים.
• לדווח באופן מיידי על כל ניסיון חשוד לגורמי האבטחה בארגון ולמוקד 119 של מערך הסייב…
warnings.ru_translation: The General Security Service and the National Cyber ​​Security Directorate are reporting an increase in attempted phishing attacks targeting Israeli journalists and others engaged in public activities. The Department and the Service have detected these attempts and are taking measures to prevent and block them. National Cybersecurity Administration guidelines for protecting accounts: • Verify the identity of the person requesting using an additional means of communication. • Do not enter passwords or verification codes into a link you receive in a message, even to join a video call. • Enable two-factor authentication for all primary accounts. • Periodically check account logins and remove unknown devices or connections. • Immediately report any suspicious attempts to your organization's security team and the National Cyber ​​Security Administration's 119 Center.
warnings.what_to_notice: In this case, attacks are aimed at journalists and public figures. Attackers may use links in messages that lead to fake login pages, especially under the pretext of joining a video call. It's important to pay attention to unexpected messages asking for a password or code, even if they look like an invitation to a video conference. You should also verify the sender's address and use additional communication channels to confirm identity.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on links or open attachments from suspicious messages
Do not provide passwords, confirmation codes or card details by phone/message
Check any charges and payment requests directly through the official website or application
If you suspect fraud, contact the National Cyber ​​Security Administration hotline 119

warnings.title: “Relative in Need” - a voice scam against Russian speakers
warnings.summary: Official confirmation from the agency: scammers purposefully call elderly Russian speakers, posing as a relative, bank or police - sometimes by faking a familiar voice through AI.
warnings.he_original: לאחרונה מתרבים ניסיונות עוקץ שמכוונים בעיקר לאוכלוסייה המבוגרת דוברת הרוסית. עבריינים מתחזים לבני משפחה, לבנק או למשטרה, ולעיתים אף מחקים קול מוכר באמצעות בינה מלאכותית
warnings.ru_translation: “Recently, fraud attempts have become more frequent, targeting mainly the elderly Russian-speaking population. Criminals impersonate family members, a bank or the police, and sometimes even imitate a familiar voice using artificial intelligence.”
warnings.what_to_notice: The agency writes directly - it is deliberately against Russian-speaking elderly people, not an accident. A voice on the phone can sound very similar to a real relative - AI has learned to imitate a voice from a short recording (for example, from a video on social networks).
what_not_to_do: Stop, hang up - do not make a decision under pressure and haste
Call a relative back directly using an already saved number, and not the one from which they called
Use a pre-agreed family code word
Never transfer money during a call

warnings.title: Fake SMS is “embedded” in real correspondence with GOV.IL
warnings.summary: Official warning about a technical trick: a fraudulent SMS with a request for payment appears on the phone in the SAME correspondence where real messages from GOV.IL usually arrive - due to the way SMS is displayed on some phone models, and not a hack of GOV.IL itself.
warnings.he_original: בשעה האחרונה מופצות הודעות SMS מתחזות עם בקשה לביצוע תשלום וקישור מזיק המופיעות בטלפון בתוך שרשור הודעות קיים של GOV.IL
warnings.ru_translation: “In the last hour, fake SMS with a request for payment and a malicious link have been spreading, which appear on the phone inside an existing correspondence with GOV.IL”
warnings.what_to_notice: The main trap is that the message looks like “our own” - it ends up in the same chat with real government SMS. The location of a message alone does NOT prove that it is real.
what_not_to_do: Do not follow the link, even if the message is in the same correspondence with real government messages
Any payment must be made only through direct access to the official website, not via a link from an SMS
Do not enter personal data or card details via the link

warnings.title: Fake “Win ​​500 ₪” giveaway on behalf of a famous brand
warnings.summary: The phishing message is disguised as a promotion from a well-known snack brand, with the promise of winning a certificate worth 500 shekels.
warnings.he_original: ההודעה נראית כמו שאלון תמים עם תמונה מוכרת של המותג, כפתורי תשובה ותגובות של "זוכים"
warnings.ru_translation: “The message looks like a harmless survey with a familiar brand image, reply buttons and comments from the “winners”
warnings.what_to_notice: Signs according to the agency’s own list: a promise of a large prize, a short survey or “draw”, a requirement to share a link on WhatsApp/Messenger, a transition to an unofficial website address. If it looks too good, it's most likely a phishing scam.
what_not_to_do: Do not enter personal or card details
Do not share a suspicious link with others
Access only official websites and official brand applications directly

warnings.title: Fake SMS on behalf of the Pango parking application - also in real correspondence
warnings.summary: Another case of the same trick: a phishing message on behalf of a popular parking payment application appears in real correspondence with this application.
warnings.he_original: מערך הסייבר הלאומי מתריע מפני הודעות פישינג המתחזות לפנגו ומופיעות בתוך שרשור ה-SMS האמיתי של החברה
warnings.ru_translation: “The Office of Cyber ​​Security is warning about phishing messages that disguise themselves as Pango and appear inside real company SMS messages.”
warnings.what_to_notice: Even if the message looks plausible and is in the right chat, this is not proof of authenticity. The only reliable way to check is to go into the application yourself, not through a link.
what_not_to_do: Do not follow a link from an SMS, even if it is in the right chat
Check accruals only through the application itself or the official website

warnings.title: Fake Israel Post website - steals data while printing
warnings.summary: A particularly dangerous scheme: a fake copy of the Israel Post website steals your entered data in real time, even before you click “send.”
warnings.he_original: המידע שמוקלד באתר מועבר לתוקפים בזמן אמת. כלומר, גם אם לא לחצתם על כפתור השליחה ולא השלמתם את התהליך, ייתכן שהפרטים שכבר הקלדתם נחשפו
warnings.ru_translation: “The information you enter on the site is transmitted to scammers in real time. That is, even if you did not click the submit button and did not complete the process, the entered data could already have been disclosed."
warnings.what_to_notice: Even the fact of printing data on a fake page is already a risk; you don’t have to press the “send” button. Before entering any data, check the exact website address, and if in doubt, check the link on special sites like scanmysms.com.
what_not_to_do: Do not click on the link in the SMS about “unsuccessful delivery” if you were not expecting the package
Check delivery status only on the official website/app of Israel Post directly
Carefully check the exact website address before entering anything.

warnings.title: “I hacked your computer” – extortion via email
warnings.summary: Mass mailing of letters threatening to publish a compromising video, allegedly recorded via a webcam, demanding a ransom.
warnings.he_original: פרצתי לך למחשב והקלטתי אותך מענג את עצמך
warnings.ru_translation: “I hacked your computer and recorded how you satisfy yourself” - the verbatim beginning of a real mailing recorded by Israel Hayom
warnings.what_to_notice: This is a classic "random" scam - sent to millions of addresses indiscriminately, no one actually hacked your device and recorded the video. The goal is to create panic and shame so that you pay without thinking.
what_not_to_do: Do not follow the attached links
Do not transfer payment, no matter how much you threaten - payment only provokes new demands
Do not enter into correspondence - save the letter as evidence, block the sender
If you have real doubts, contact 119 rather than resolve the issue yourself

warnings.title: Fake “invoice” letter with hidden remote access program
warnings.summary: An email supposedly from a well-known billing service, with a link to “download an invoice” - in fact, the link leads to installing a program for remote access to a computer.
warnings.he_original: מבדיקת המערך עולה כי הקישור מפנה להורדת ScreenConnect, כלי לגישה מרחוק המשמש לרוב למטרות לגיטימיות, אך במקרה זה זוהה כחלק ממתווה תקיפה זדוני
warnings.ru_translation: “Based on a management review, the link is a download for ScreenConnect, a remote access program that is typically used for legitimate purposes, but in this case was identified as part of a malicious attack pattern.”
warnings.what_to_notice: The remote access program itself is not malicious; it is used, for example, by technical support. The danger is precisely that they are trying to establish it by deception, through a letter that you did not expect.
what_not_to_do: Carefully check letters about invoices/invoices, especially if you were not expecting them
Do not follow links or download files from suspicious emails
Do not confirm installation of remote access programs from unsolicited emails
Keep your antivirus and system updated

warnings.title: A real example of a fake website address in SMS
warnings.summary: Documented case: SMS with vague “bureaucratic” text and a link to an obviously fake website address.
warnings.ru_translation: “Following the annual data update, you are invited to view the updated review status of your account. Secure login to your personal account: trsom.xyz"
warnings.what_to_notice: Look at the address itself: “trsom.xyz” is in no way connected with real government websites (those end in .gov.il), and the ending “.xyz” is almost never used by official Israeli institutions. The name "trsom" is meaningless. Plus the text itself is vague - it doesn’t name any real department.
what_not_to_do: Check the website address carefully - real Israeli government websites end in .gov.il
Do not click on a link if the message is vague and does not name a specific agency
Access the desired site directly through search
